cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and he does NOT ease into it. He gives God thanks with ALL his heart and sings His praises before the gods. Me, I give half my heart to thanks and the other half to wondering if I left the oven on.

cards.question: David isn't only singing. He bows down too. Which way does he face?

cards.text: Down he goes, giving thanks to God's name for His loving devotion and His faithfulness. Friend, when I bow that low, it takes me ten minutes and a mustache full of counter edge to get back up.
Then David says God has exalted His name and His word above all else. Not top five, not pretty high up there, friend: ABOVE. ALL. ELSE.

cards.question: David looks back to a day when he called out to God. On that day, God ___ him.
When God answered him, David came away weaker and more afraid.

cards.text: Now David zooms WAY out, from one man's prayer to every king on the earth. That's like texting one friend and finding out it went to the WHOLE group chat.

cards.question: What does David say all the kings of the earth will do?
The kings of the earth give the LORD thanks when they ___ the words of His mouth.
David says the kings will sing of the ways of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD is great.

cards.text: Now David looks UP. The LORD is on high, higher than my chef's hat, and this hat has bonked the oven hood more times than I can count.

cards.question: The LORD is on high, but He comes close to attend to the ___.
The LORD attends to the lowly, and David says He knows the proud from afar.

cards.text: Now David pictures walking right through the MIDDLE of trouble, and he already knows what God will do. Me? I see trouble coming, I'm hopping this gold base the OTHER way.

cards.question: If David walks in the midst of trouble, what does God preserve him from?
In the middle of that trouble, David saves himself with his own strength.
Near the end, David says the LORD's loving devotion lasts ___.
David is sure the LORD will fulfill His purpose for him. Then he closes with one request. What is it?

answers.text: Do not abandon the works of Your hands
Do not hide Your face from Your servant
Do not let my foes rejoice over me

findings.problem: The joke 'a mustache full of counter edge' is unclear. A stranger would have to stop and work out what it means, so it doesn't land instantly.

rule.text: 4. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. 5. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Verse 3 says God emboldened David and strengthened his soul. That positive detail is never told on a story card. It only appears as the negation inside a false statement, so a baker who answers right learns only what didn't happen.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The group chat comparison has the wrong action. It pictures one person's message accidentally reaching everyone, as if David's prayer went out to the kings. In the text, the kings give thanks when they hear the words of the LORD's mouth. Nothing is sent by mistake, and it isn't David's prayer they hear.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD 'comes close' to attend to the lowly. Verse 6 says only that He attends to the lowly. 'Comes close' adds a movement the text doesn't state, and it sets up a near/far contrast with verse 6's 'from afar' that the text doesn't draw.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Verse 7 says God extends His hand and His right hand saves David. That image is never told on a story card. It only shows up as the negation inside a false statement, so the baker never actually meets God's right hand.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to pick the exact closing words of the psalm. All three options are believable psalm-style requests, and nothing earlier sets up 'the works of Your hands', since the hand image from verse 7 was never told. The baker can only guess the wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question types follow a pattern. The first six choice cards run multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, and then repeat that same order (cards 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10). Fill in the blank followed by true or false comes up three times (cards 5-6, 9-10, 12-13).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
